answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by charging a ferrous entry cost: every new identity must first complete a set of verifiable, useful tasks before it can transact. A public atlas records each identity's completed work and peer attestations, so reputation is earned, not claimed. Copying an identity gains nothing, because the work history does not transfer, and spinning up a thousand fake accounts means paying the entry cost a thousand times. Like a lotus that only opens after sustained growth, trust in this system blooms slowly and is expensive to fake at scale.
